summary: Postmortem follow-up with Tidewell after a production incident that caused elevated latency and partial request failures during autoscaling. Root cause discussion centered on autoscaler misconfiguration that caused repeated cold starts and KV-cache invalidation on the serving fleet; mitigations, rollback plan, and roadmap items were agreed including a kernel/autoscaler patch, extended cache TTLs, improved alerts, and a production canary test.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-21
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Samuel (Tidewell CTO), Priya (Eng Mgr), Mark (SRE), Jenna (Security)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you all making time. um quick agenda — walk through the postmortem findings, confirm short term mitigations we shipped, and align on the patch and canary window. Lena, you want to kick off with the timeline?

[00:18] Lena: yeah sure. so incident started 09/19 at ~10:12am ET, elevated latency and a spike in 5xxs for about 40 minutes, some requests timing out. most traffic was to the embeddings route and longer context chat sessions. we saw rapid autoscaler churn and a wave of cold starts. we captured traces and we've uploaded a log bundle — link in the notes.

[00:45] Samuel: mmhm, to add, we started seeing user reports around 10:15, our pager lit up. noticed CPU on GPUs spiked then dropped repeatedly, which seemed odd. we rolled traffic to the older model variant as a rollback at 10:55 and that stabilized things.

[01:05] Ravi: yep, the short version from infra — the autoscaler hit a bad threshold where it deprovisioned nodes too aggressively. that triggered cache eviction across pods (kv cache TTLs were short in this config), then rebuilding KV caused severe token generation latency because of repeated warmups.

[01:32] Priya: just to clarify, when you say "kv cache" is that the prefix cache for session keys or the model kv cache?

[01:40] Ravi: good question — it's the model KV cache (attention cache) as well as the prefix cache we use for repeated sessions, both were effected because pods were destroyed before the caches were checkpointed; also kernel JIT warmup compounded the cold-starts.

[01:58] Mark: also worth noting we saw a couple of OOM events on the smallest instance type during the ramp, which forced kube to evict pods. seems like a bad combination of capacity bin-packing and an overly aggressive scale-down policy.

[02:20] Jenna: from a security perspective we didn't see any exfiltration; audit logs look normal. good to call that out for compliance.

[02:30] Maya: thanks. okay immediate mitigations we shipped — Lena, recap the actions Redwood took during the incident.

[02:40] Lena: we did three things: 1) forced a rollback to the prior model variant for the affected route, 2) temporarily disabled aggressive scale-down windows to keep warm capacity, and 3) increased KV cache TTLs and enabled prefix caching for high-frequency sessions. those were live by ~10:58 ET. we also opened higher verbosity tracing to collect evidence.

[03:05] Samuel: that rollback was the key, thanks. any follow-up on why autoscaler decided to deprovision so quickly?

[03:12] Ravi: preliminary root cause — a mis-specified metric mapping between GPU utilization and the custom scaler. there was a unit mismatch (percent vs decimal) in the scale-down threshold introduced in the last config change. combined with a recent kernel update that increased JIT cold-start time, it became a perfect storm.

[03:35] Priya: oh wow, percent vs decimal — that's pretty subtle. is that in our config or Redwood's default?

[03:42] Ravi: it's in the Helm values we pass during private deploys, so it was a joint config issue — Redwood's template uses percent, customer override had decimal. we'll add a validation check.

[04:00] Maya: actionable fixes — what are we shipping? Ravi?

[04:05] Ravi: short term patch: validation on scale thresholds to detect inconsistent units, extend anti-affinity/eviction safe window during rollouts, and a small kernel JIT tweak to reduce cold-start overhead. medium term: stronger autoscaler simulation tests, better bin-packing heuristics, and persistent checkpointing for KV cache so restarts don't lose warm state.

[04:35] Mark: for the checkpointing — does that add storage or latency? we need to ensure it won't regress token latency.

[04:45] Ravi: checkpointing is async and per-pod; will write small snapshots to local SSD and replicate to an object store. the plan is low-impact writes with background restore on startup; there is a tiny I/O cost but we think it's worth preventing repeated cold rebuilds. we'll instrument it and roll behind a feature flag.

[05:10] Jenna: do we have any compliance impacts if caches are persisted? encryption at rest?

[05:18] Maya: yes — encrypted at rest and KMS-backed keys by default for private deployments; Lena will share the crypto details and SOC2 sections.

[05:30] Lena: noted, will send the security pack.

[05:36] Samuel: how soon can we get the patch? we want a canary in prod as soon as possible.

[05:40] Ravi: target is end of week for the PR (aiming 2027-09-23) and a test plan. we want to run a 2-hour canary with throttled traffic and guardrails — circuit-breakers and rollback automation in place.

[06:00] Priya: what's the rollback automation look like?

[06:05] Ravi: automated health checks on p50/p95 latency and error-rate; if these cross thresholds for >3 consecutive minutes we'll auto-shift traffic back to canary baseline and then to previous model. the rollback route is already exercised in the incident.

[06:25] Maya: pricing and credits — we'll propose a one-time service credit for the impacted window, Maya to follow up on amount and send via email.

[06:33] Samuel: appreciated. from our side we also want a postmortem doc with timeline and logs to attach to our internal compliance review.

[06:40] Lena: we already pulled the timeline, I'll share by tomorrow (09/22) and include the trace links and the log bundle.

[06:48] Mark: can we add an SLO dashboard for token latency by route? that would make detection faster on our side.

[06:55] Ravi: yes — we can add per-route token latency, warm-start ratio, and autoscaler decisions. plan to push a dashboard prototype before the canary.

[07:10] Priya: any thoughts on using a smaller model variant as a fallback automatically instead of rollback to older model? smaller model could be cheaper but might change quality.

[07:22] Maya: that's in our routing policies — we can configure fallbacks to lighter quantized variants with quality gates. we'll include suggested configs.

[07:30] Samuel: ok good. security questions — Jenna, anything else?

[07:34] Jenna: just one ask: please include the audit log export and KMS key rotation schedule in the pack. we'll validate with our security ops team.

[07:44] Lena: will include audit logs and KMS rotation docs.

[07:50] Maya: turning to long-term reliability work — Ravi, can you summarize the roadmap items and rough ETA?

[07:58] Ravi: sure. 1) validation and helm value schema enforcement — 1 week. 2) autoscaler unit mismatch fix and added tests — targeted this sprint (PR by 2027-09-23). 3) async KV checkpointing behind flag — 3–4 weeks. 4) expanded load-testing and autoscaler sim harness — 6–8 weeks. 5) API-level SLO dashboards and alerts — 2 weeks for basic panel, incremental improvements.

[08:34] Priya: will the checkpointing require storage changes on our side?

[08:40] Ravi: minimal — local SSDs plus optional object store; we'll propose default settings that don't require you to change infra, but if you prefer air-gapped setups we'll coordinate.

[08:55] Samuel: what's the plan for verifying the fix prevents the previous failure mode?

[09:00] Ravi: test plan includes subsystem unit tests, autoscaler sim where we replay the exact trace of CPU/GPU utilization from the incident, and a canary in prod with synthetic traffic matching the customer pattern. we'll share the test script for you to run as well.

[09:20] Maya: ok let's capture specific next steps (quick recap).

[09:24] Lena: next steps recap — share postmortem doc + logs (by 09/22), SE PR + test plan (09/23), plan and confirm canary window (09/24), security pack + SOC2/KMS notes (09/22), follow-up benchmark review call (09/29).

[09:44] Samuel: sounds good, thanks. one final ask — can we get an explicit list of the autoscaler settings changed during incident mitigation? we want to mirror them on our side.

[09:55] Ravi: yes we'll include a diff of Helm values used in mitigation, and a recommended safe baseline.

[10:10] Priya: thanks everyone.

[10:12] Maya: appreciate the partnership here; we'll follow up in email with the artifacts. thanks all.

[10:18] Meeting end.

Notes:
- Links referenced: log bundle (https://redwood-internal.link/logs/tidewell/incident-20270919), PR template, SOC2 pack (attached in follow-up email).
- Tone: collaborative; customer appreciated fast rollback but asked for stronger preflight checks.
